For each canonical ID, retain the row with greatest numeric timestamp among VALID rows. Canonical ID trims surrounding spaces and casefolds letters. Do not let a later INVALID row erase an earlier valid one. Public examples must show actual version-specific usable workflow and complete resulting records, not merely a row count. Any equivalent owned transformation meeting this semantic result and the destination schema is accepted. No new binary build is commissioned.

BIN-232 /2.3.2 LTS accepts CSV fields id,t,value,valid with valid encoded1/0, not JSON. With selected flags its fixed order is exact-raw-ID dedupe keeping FIRST, then trim/casefold canonicalization, then valid-only filtering; command argument order does not change stages. Flags --canonical-id,--valid-only,--dedupe=first are supported; no --valid-first override. Prepared CSV may be imported without flags. BIN-240 /2.4 accepts JSON fields id,t,reading,valid with Boolean true/false. Its default selected-flag order is canonicalization, dedupe keeping NEWEST timestamp, then valid-only filtering. Supported --valid-first changes this to canonicalization, valid-only filter, dedupe/newest. Flags --canonical-id,--valid-only,--valid-first,--dedupe=newest supported. A newest documentation edit date changes neither binary schema nor stage order.
